description: Headless GIMP: write a deliverable to disk — every live filter is baked in, and ALL metadata (EXIF/XMP/IPTC/GPS, thumbnail) is stripped unconditionally, never carried over from the source. Format is picked from the file_path extension: jpg/jpeg, png, webp and tif/tiff write a FLATTENED image; psd writes a LAYERED file for finishing in Photoshop or another editor. In a PSD, layers keep their masks, opacity, blend modes, visibility and groups; filters are baked into each layer; a group with its own filter is merged into one layer; text layers become pixels. Photoshop blends partly transparent layers and blend modes in gamma space, so those can look slightly different there — the result lists them. Any other extension is refused, and .xcf is refused outright — use gimp_save_xcf for the live, re-editable document instead. Refuses to overwrite an existing file unless overwrite: true (with it, the existing file is replaced). A flattened image is composited onto white by default; keep_alpha: true (png or webp only) keeps transparency, so a cut-out exports with a transparent background. The color profile is not metadata and is kept: a wide-gamut photo (an iPhone's Display P3) is written with its profile embedded unless color_profile converts it, and the result reports the space written.

bit_depth.description: PNG/TIFF/PSD only: output bit depth. JPEG/WebP are always 8-bit.

color_profile.description: 'keep' writes the image in its own color space with that profile embedded, so a phone's Display P3 photo keeps its full color. 'srgb' converts to sRGB first, the safest choice for viewers that ignore profiles; 'adobe-rgb' converts to Adobe RGB (RGB images only). Plain sRGB is written with no profile, which viewers assume.

file_path.description: Absolute path. The extension picks the format: jpg/jpeg, png, webp, tif/tiff (flattened), or psd (layered). Refuses .xcf outright — that is gimp_save_xcf's job. Metadata (EXIF/XMP/IPTC/GPS, thumbnail) is ALWAYS stripped on export, unconditionally — never carried over from the source.

image.description: Image id, as returned by gimp_open_document.

keep_alpha.description: PNG/WebP only: keep transparency. The visible layers are merged onto a transparent canvas, so areas no layer covers (a cut-out, say) stay transparent. Default false flattens onto white. Refused for JPEG and TIFF.

lossless.description: WebP only: lossless encoding. Ignored for other formats.

overwrite.description: Refuses to overwrite an existing file unless true.

png_compression.description: PNG only: compression level, 0 (fastest, largest) to 9 (slowest, smallest). GIMP's own default of 9 measured far slower for negligible size gain on a typical photo, hence the lower default here. Ignored for other formats.

quality.description: JPEG/WebP quality, 1-100 (higher = better/larger). Ignored for png/tiff. WebP itself accepts 0 too, but JPEG's own bound is 1-100, so this schema uses the tighter bound.

tiff_compression.description: TIFF only: compression scheme (lzw and adobe_deflate are lossless; jpeg is lossy). Ignored for other formats.

name: gimp_export

color_profile.description: The image's color space: space is srgb, display-p3, dci-p3, adobe-rgb, prophoto-rgb, rec2020, gray or other; name is the profile's own name (null for plain sRGB); wide_gamut is true when the space holds colors sRGB cannot show.

layers.description: PSD only: layers written, groups included.

may_blend_differently.description: PSD only: visible layers below 100% opacity or with a non-normal blend mode.

merged_groups.description: PSD only: groups merged into one layer to keep their own filter.

rasterized_text.description: PSD only: text layers written as pixels.
